purpose: Behavior guards for PART-02 and PART-03's candidate-page edits (D14, GUARD-001). Forbidden guards are a broad match minus named exceptions, so surviving old text fails them (D26-E, SCOPE-001); required guards prove the repair text is present. They become candidate registry assertions in PART-07 for every member with a registry row.
semantics: A unit is a line, or a sentence within a line (split after . ! or ? followed by whitespace). A unit matches when every `all` pattern matches it and no `except` pattern does. A forbidden guard passes at 0 matching units; a required guard passes at exactly `expect` matching units per prompt. Fixtures expand every @KEY shared text from edits.json. Only counts are reported (D22).
fixture_rule: Fixtures are synthetic text, not prompt bodies. Each `pass` fixture must satisfy the guard and each `fail` fixture must violate it; a guard whose fail fixture passes has never fired (GUARD-001). A `fail_count_only` fixture is a required guard's count above `expect`: the guard must fail it, and its registry form, which proves presence only, passes it; the registry row carries its own assertion for that case (G-MGMT-2: mgmt10-registry-row.json's duplicate Prompt ID assertion).
